column4: An artifact carries compile-time macros so a caller can #if on a fact rather than read an rx_info field at run time (D46: every strategy selection point is observable).
The compile-time macro mirror of rx_info is PARTIAL: on a VM artifact six of rx_info's fifteen fields have a macro and nine do not.
rx_info.ncaps is mirrored by the macro <PREFIX>_NCAPS.
rx_info.engine is mirrored by <PREFIX>_ENGINE, as the string "vm" on a VM artifact.
rx_info.engine_why is mirrored by <PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY.
rx_info.step_budget is mirrored by <PREFIX>_STEP_BUDGET.
rx_info.work_budget is mirrored by <PREFIX>_WORK_BUDGET.
rx_info.frame_capacity is mirrored by <PREFIX>_BT_FRAMES.
rx_info fields abi, flags, encoding, ngroups, nnames, subject_ceiling, pattern, pattern_len and groups have no compile-time macro.
rx_info.ngroups has no macro, so it is reachable only by reading <prefix>_info at run time (unlike ncaps, which has <PREFIX>_NCAPS).
Selection facts (family (a): which engine, which candidate-start mechanism) are unconditional: present on every artifact pcrec emits, with an engine-appropriate value.
The M2.1 self-loop skip is a scan-avoidance mechanism that is not yet stamped.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE is stamped on both artifact kinds, as "vm" or "dfa", from one emitter (pcrec_emit_engine_stamp) so the two spellings cannot drift.

The prefilter axis keeps engine-specific macro names because its value sets are different vocabularies: <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER is the VM's; <PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER and <PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN are the DFA scan's.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE is on every artifact pcrec emits, without exception.
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN and <PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER are on every artifact that CONTAINS a DFA scan: every DFA artifact and every VM hybrid.

A VM hybrid (<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "hybrid") inlines the DFA emitter's own forward+reverse or attempt scan as a static function with its own tables, its own D11 bound and its own candidate-start filter.
A non-hybrid VM artifact contains no DFA scan and carries neither <PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN nor <PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER.
IFF: a VM artifact carries the two _DFA_* macros (_DFA_SCAN, _DFA_PREFILTER) if and only if <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER is "hybrid".
tests/codegen/run_dfa_stamps.sh asserts the hybrid <=> _DFA_* IFF in both directions, using the emitted static <prefix>_prefilter body as the independent third term.
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER and <PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER are two different selections, not two spellings of one.
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER says whether the VM runs a capture-erased DFA ahead of its program at all.
<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER says what candidate-start filter the DFA scan itself carries.
A hybrid artifact answers both _VM_PREFILTER and _DFA_PREFILTER, and the two answers are independent.
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG is a third independent selection question beside _VM_PREFILTER and _DFA_PREFILTER, not a refinement of either: which LANGUAGE the prefilter DFA recognises.
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG has exactly two values, "exact" and "count-collapsed".
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG "exact" means the count-collapse axis did not fire: the prefilter is not a count-collapsed superset (it may still over-approximate for another reason).

<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG "count-collapsed" means the prefilter recognises a count-collapsed superset: every A_REP with rmin > 1 or rmax > 1 is lowered as X{min(rmin,1),} so the machine does not scale with the count.
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG is present on every artifact whose VM prefilter decision came out "hybrid", i.e. exactly where <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER reads "hybrid".
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG is on no DFA artifact at all, because a DFA artifact takes no VM prefilter decision.
The _VM_PREFILTER_LANG scope (hybrid only) is narrower than the _DFA_* family's scope (contains a DFA scan, which a plain DFA artifact also satisfies).
tests/codegen/run_dfa_stamps.sh asserts the _VM_PREFILTER_LANG IFF in both directions.
A prefilter is a filter and its contract is unchanged by the _VM_PREFILTER_LANG value: its rejection is sound and its span START is a lower bound the VM verifies from.
The artifact's answers are identical under _VM_PREFILTER_LANG "exact" and "count-collapsed" (the axis is answer-identity-preserving, D46).
A count-collapsed superset cannot supply an upper bound on the match end, so a "count-collapsed" artifact always reads <PREFIX>_VM_PRUNE_CEILING "subject-end".
The "count-collapsed" => "subject-end" consequence is the same one an atomic group or a lookaround already has.
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG has no rx_info mirror, on <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE's precedent; the trigger to add one is a named consumer, not symmetry (D77).
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG reports the count-collapse axis ONLY (D142).
<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG "exact" does NOT say the prefilter recognises the pattern's own language.
A lookbehind, lookahead, atomic group or \K is erased from the prefilter's machine, which then over-approximates while _VM_PREFILTER_LANG still reads "exact".
Measured on 76 lookbehind, 47 lookahead, 132 atomic and 53 \K hybrids (docs/design/pf_know.md section 2.2/8.4): the prefilter over-approximates while _VM_PREFILTER_LANG reads "exact".
Whether a successful prefilter also proves the match END is read from <PREFIX>_VM_RESEED: its "exact" row is the one where the prefilter answers for the pattern's own language.
No stamp line is added to report whether the prefilter recognises the pattern's own language beyond _VM_RESEED.
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED reports what the hybrid's retry does after a failed attempt.
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED has the same IFF as _VM_PREFILTER_LANG: present on every artifact whose _VM_PREFILTER reads "hybrid", and no other.
The <PREFIX>_VM_RESEED value is the name of the first-match row that fired; pcrec --list-axes prints the table under axis hyb-reseed.
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED "exact": the prefilter answers for the pattern's own language, so a failed attempt cannot follow one of its answers; the retry is the one emitted before abi 49.
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED "clamped": over-approximating prefilter on an artifact with an MRL clamp; the pre-abi-49 retry, which already re-seeds after every failed attempt.

<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED "anchored": over-approximating clamp-free prefilter on a start-anchored pattern (_VM_START not "unanchored"); the attempt loop stops after its first attempt, no retry runs, and the pre-abi-49 retry's text is emitted.

<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED "adaptive-dense": over-approximating clamp-free prefilter where the compile's byte-rate prior predicts dense candidates; the retry steps or re-seeds per call, starting in step mode.
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED "adaptive": over-approximating clamp-free prefilter; the retry steps or re-seeds per call, starting with a short step budget.
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED "fixed": -fno-hyb-reseed on an over-approximating clamp-free prefilter; the pre-abi-49 retry.
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED is a selection fact emitted under _VM_PREFILTER_LANG's IFF rather than unconditionally.
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED has no rx_info mirror (D77).
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED describes run time only: every value answers identically, except that an adaptive* artifact can answer where the pre-abi-49 retry gave up on a budget.
<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD reports what the entries do with a caller's mid-character position.
<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD is unconditional: on every artifact of both engines, a family (a) selection fact riding the shared prologue, because the axis belongs to the entries.
<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD "guarded": a startpos (or ctx->pos) > 0 inside a character is refused with PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS; the default under an encoding with multi-byte characters.
<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD "align": (-fstartpos-guard=align) such a position is moved forward to the next character start once at entry; an anchored entry answers -1.
<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD "permissive": the artifact answers at whatever position the caller named; arises from -fno-startpos-guard, or an encoding (byte) where every position is a character start.
<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK reports whether the entries refuse an ill-formed subject.
<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK is unconditional, on every artifact, beside _STARTPOS_GUARD.
<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK "whole": (-futf-check) every entry that takes a subject refuses with PCREC_ERR_UTF when an ill-formed sequence begins in [startpos - LB, n).
<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK "off": the default; invalid-tolerant, an ill-formed sequence matches nothing and is not reported.
<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK "inert": the encoding has no ill-formed byte strings (byte); no check exists whatever was asked.
<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD and <PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK are each read off the same predicate the emitted entry text is, so a stamp and its body cannot disagree.
Neither <PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD nor <PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK has an rx_info mirror (D77).
rx_info.flags carries the two UTF-check/startpos-guard request bits, masked out where inert.
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE is a third _DFA_* macro, under the same IFF as _DFA_SCAN/_DFA_PREFILTER: present on every artifact that contains a DFA scan (every DFA artifact and every VM hybrid), and no other.
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE names the encoding of the DFA scan's transition table.
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE "premultiplied": every numeric transition table in the artifact's DFA scan holds next_state * classes, so the emitted step is state = table[state + class].
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE "indexed": every numeric transition table holds next_state and the step multiplies (the form emitted before OPT-3).

<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE "mixed": the machines the artifact contains took different forms; the choice is per machine, on that machine's own states * classes and seed table (a machine that can start dead for some context byte is indexed).
The machines considered by <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE are the forward one, the reverse one unless the search is start-pinned, and the anchored one under <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped".
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE "none": the scan has no numeric transition table at all: _DFA_SCAN "attempt" (states are labels, a step is a computed goto) or _DFA_SCAN "empty".
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE is a family (a) selection fact, read off the same predicate the emitted loop branches on.
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE names the selection that was MADE; after the uniform fold an artifact can carry that selection without carrying a table.
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS is where a consumer reads how many DFA tables are actually present.
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE does NOT fall to "none" when every table folds; the representation was still chosen.
The representation fixes the folded constant's value: 65535 under "premultiplied", -1 under "indexed".
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE "none" means a scan with no numeric transition table by construction (_DFA_SCAN "attempt" or "empty"), not a fully folded scan.
<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE has no rx_info mirror, deliberately.
Unlike scan and prefilter, whose rx_info mirrors tuning.md section 3.2 records, <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE has no rx_info field.
Section 6.3's (a)/(b) split is a rule about macros and makes the macro owed; the rx_info struct fields are a separate layout decision.
Trigger: the first consumer that reads rx_info.scan or rx_info.prefilter at run time makes a table mirror owed too, as an append at the end of the struct that moves no existing offset.
There are three rx_info mirrors of a DFA selection stamp (scan, prefilter, match_form) plus search_form as the fourth field; table is not one of them.
rx_info.scan and rx_info.prefilter are mirrors of a DFA selection stamp (DD-13c, abi 6).
rx_info.match_form mirrors a DFA selection stamp (ENG-ABS, abi 10).
rx_info.search_form mirrors a DFA selection stamp (OPT-5 STEP 2, abi 16).
match_form and search_form mirror caller-visible COST properties of an entry point the caller calls, whereas table and scan_edge are internal encoding choices with no rx_info mirror.
rx_info.search_form's guard is scan/prefilter's, not match_form's: a hybrid inlines this emitter's search body, so it has a search form to report.

The four DFA stamp values (_DFA_SCAN, _DFA_PREFILTER, _DFA_TABLE, _DFA_SCAN_EDGE family) come from one derivation per engine (unanch_start, attempt_cand in src/gen/emit_dfa.c) read by every site that needs them: emitted loop, DFA stamp, hybrid stamp.
A DFA-derived stamp cannot disagree with the loop it describes unless the derivation itself is wrong, in which case the loop is wrong too.
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS is a fourth _DFA_* macro, under the same IFF as _DFA_TABLE: present on every artifact that contains a DFA scan (every DFA artifact and every VM hybrid), and no other.
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS is an INTEGER, not a string (e.g. #define RX_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS 4).
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS is the number of the artifact's DFA tables whose cells were all equal and which are therefore NOT EMITTED; the accessor returns the constant instead.
Two tables per machine are foldable, <m>_next_state and <m>_is_accepting, so <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS runs 0..6.
The forward machine is always counted in <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS.
The reverse machine is counted in <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS unless the search is start-pinned (it is not in the artifact to fold).
The anchored machine is counted in <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS under <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped".
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS, _DFA_TABLE and _DFA_SCAN_EDGE use the same machine composition, so none can name a machine the artifact does not contain.
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS is 0 on _DFA_SCAN "attempt" and "empty", which have neither table.
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS is a COUNT and deliberately not a MASK: it is a whole-artifact total with no per-quantifier axis to mix.
Other masks in section 6.3 are masks because a rung, strategy or clamp is chosen per A_REP and a scalar would lie on a mixed artifact.
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS is family (b) (a fact about what the emitted machine turned out to contain), for <PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS's reason.
There is no fold mode anywhere upstream of the emitter; the fold is discovered while the emitter has the table in hand.
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS is owed rather than optional, because the fold's effect is a table's absence and a fact readable only by a macro's absence is not an acceptable discriminator.
tests/codegen/run_dfa_uniform_fold.sh reads <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS.
A consumer may conclude from <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS that the artifact is smaller and its scan loop cheaper by that many indexed loads.
A consumer may NOT conclude anything about the answers from <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS: they are identical either way, a uniform table and its constant being the same function.
<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS has no rx_info mirror, on <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE's precedent, because no consumer reads the fact at run time today (D77).
The trigger that would make an rx_info mirror of <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS owed is the one _DFA_TABLE's entry names, and it would be a struct append moving no existing offset.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW reports how far from the subject's end a match may begin.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW is a family (a) stamp: on every artifact pcrec emits, both engines, because the analysis is neither engine's.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW "4" (a decimal string) means a match begins in [n - 4, n].
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW "none" means nothing was proved.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW is a string with a "none" member, not a number with a sentinel, because 0 is a legal window (a \z pattern of maximum width 0 may begin only at the subject's end).
The <PREFIX>_END_WINDOW value is the bound both search entries clamp to, emitted from the same compile-time field as the clamp itself.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW is "none" for a pattern that is not end-anchored.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW is "none" for a pattern whose width is unbounded.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW is "none" for a pattern containing \G.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW is "none" for a pattern under a multi-byte encoding.
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW is "none" for an artifact built with -fno-end-window.
A consumer may conclude that a non-"none" <PREFIX>_END_WINDOW artifact does constant work on an arbitrarily long subject.
A consumer may NOT read <PREFIX>_END_WINDOW "none" as "this pattern is not end-anchored".
<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW has no rx_info mirror, on <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE's precedent, because no consumer reads the fact at run time today (D77).
<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE reports a byte every match must contain.
<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE is a family (a) stamp: on every artifact pcrec emits, both engines.
<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE "62" (decimal byte value string) means every match contains the byte '>'.
<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE "none" means no byte is necessary on every path.
<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE is a string with a "none" member because 0 is a legal byte value, so no number is free to mean "declined".

The <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE value is the member of the necessary set a subject is least likely to contain, by the resolved analysis's byte-rate answer, with the rightmost rule as tiebreak and as the whole answer where the answer is NONE.
Where the OPT-REQPOS RUN shipped (tuning.md 2.28) and its scan member is an exact byte, <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE is that member.
Where the run's scan member is a two-member cube (tuning.md 2.39), <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE is the set's pick, or "none" for an empty set.
Every <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE value is a member of the necessary set.
A consumer may conclude that a non-"none" <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE artifact rejects a whole subject in one pass when the byte is absent, provided <PREFIX>_REQ_WHY reads "emitted".
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY is the stamp that says whether the <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE fact was acted on.
A consumer may NOT read <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE "none" as "this pattern has no required literal": it is the safe answer of a conservative analysis.
A caselessly folded literal, an alternation with no common byte, and -fno-req-byte all report <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE "none".
<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE has no rx_info mirror, on <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE's precedent, because no consumer reads the fact at run time today (D77).
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN reports a literal run every match must contain.
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN is a family (a) stamp: on every artifact pcrec emits, both engines.
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN "2e746172@0" means every match contains ".tar" and the emitted memchr scans member 0 ('.').
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN "53454c454354@4/dfdfdfdfdfdf" (for (?i)select) means every match contains a member of each position with (x & K) == T, and the scan is the pair at position 4.
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN "none" means no run of two or more bytes.
The <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN value is the run's bytes as lowercase hex, then '@', then the index within the run of the member the emitted memchr scans for.
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN is "none" at a run length below 2, which is <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE's own case.
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN uses hex because a run is arbitrary bytes inside a #define's string body.
<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE is exactly bytes[idx] of <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN wherever position idx is an exact byte, which makes the two stamps checkable against each other.
Since abi 59, a <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN run whose positions are not all exact bytes carries '/' and each position's mask K in hex.
In a masked <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN, T (the bytes) is each position's lower member and (x & K) == T is its membership test.
An exact <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN run's text is unchanged by the mask suffix (no '/' part).
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN has no rx_info mirror, for its sibling's reason.
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY reports whether the artifact acted on either required-byte/required-run fact, and why not.
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY is a closed four-token selection stamp, family (a): on every artifact pcrec emits, both engines.
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY has exactly four values: "emitted", "none", "one-attempt", "dominated".
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "emitted": the artifact emits a pre-check on the byte or run its two siblings (_REQ_BYTE, _REQ_RUN) name.
Since abi 60, a <PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "emitted" pre-check may be LED by a rarer necessary-set byte's one-byte check; the stamp says whether, not in which shape.
Since abi 61, a <PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "emitted" pre-check may be HANDED OFF (see <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF).
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "none": nothing is necessary, no byte and no run (the analysis found neither, or -fno-req-byte denied them).
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "one-attempt": declined because the search route tries ONE start position, so a whole-window pass in front of it can only add work.
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "dominated": declined because the artifact's own candidate-start memchr already scans a byte at least as rare.
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY is "none" if and only if <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE and <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN are both "none" (since abi 59).
Any <PREFIX>_REQ_WHY value other than "none" asserts that a byte or a run WAS derived; only "emitted" asserts that the artifact tests it.
A consumer asking whether an artifact rejects a subject in one pass reads <PREFIX>_REQ_WHY first and then _REQ_BYTE/_REQ_RUN for the value, never the siblings alone.
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY has no rx_info mirror, its siblings' reason.
<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF (abi 61) reports where the search body's scan begins.
<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF is a family (a) stamp: on every artifact pcrec emits, both engines.
A stamp varies by engine family, never by presence within one; "does not apply" is a value (Frank's ruling, 2026-10-05).
<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF "2" (a decimal K) means the scan begins K bytes before the run pre-check's first window hit.
<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF "none" means the scan begins at startpos.
<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF is a decimal K only where the req-use table's handoff row applies (tuning.md 2.41).
A <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF decimal value requires an emitted run pre-check (<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "emitted" with a <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN).
A <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF decimal value requires a DFA scan in front of the body (a DFA artifact, or a VM hybrid's prefilter).
A <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF decimal value requires a finite K.
A <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF decimal value requires a prefilter that is not count-collapsed.
A <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF decimal value is excluded for a VM hybrid with a \G start family whose prefilter window is its match ceiling.
Under a decimal <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF, every match begins at most K bytes before an occurrence of the run's window.
Under a decimal <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF, the pre-check's search block returns the LEAST position >= startpos at which the whole window occurs, or n when none does.
A caller of the pre-check's search block may use the returned position, not only its comparison with n.
Under a decimal <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF, the body begins its scan at max(startpos, hit - K), rounded up to a character start under a multibyte encoding when it moved.
<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF is "none" everywhere else, including every artifact built -fno-req-handoff.
The <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF K is the req_run_maxoff fact --emit-facts lists (facts_listing.md), in BYTES.
(?i)straße under -e utf8 reads <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF "2", because (?i)s matches U+017F (two bytes) before the window TRA.
A non-"none" <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF never changes an answer or a give-up; it says the artifact skips positions a necessary literal proved cannot begin a match.
<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF has no rx_info mirror, its siblings' reason.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN (abi 62) reports where a VM attempt can start.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN is a family (a) stamp: on every artifact pcrec emits, both engines, beside <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF and for its ruling.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN "first-class" means attempts start only where the byte is in the start set.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN "none" means every position is attempted.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN is "first-class" where the candidate table's VM-route row applies (tuning.md 2.42).
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN "first-class" requires a VM artifact with no DFA prefilter (<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none").
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN "first-class" requires an unanchored pattern.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN "first-class" requires a start set (the start_set fact --emit-facts lists) that cannot match empty and has fewer than 256 members.
Under <PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN "first-class", the attempt loop seeks the next byte of the start set through a 256-entry table before its first attempt and after each failed one.
Under <PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN "first-class", the artifact answers no-match where no start-set byte is left.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN is "none" on every DFA artifact.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN is "none" on every VM hybrid (whose prefilter is its start test).
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN is "none" on every anchored or \G-start pattern.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN is "none" on every artifact built -fno-start-set.
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN names the FORM of the seek; a one-byte (memchr) form is not built.
A non-"none" <PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN never changes an answer; a give-up may become the answer (section 3.1).
<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN has no rx_info mirror, its siblings' reason.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS reports which findings this artifact was built from.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS is a family (a) stamp: on every artifact, both engines.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS "byte-rate=default:1822fb973b95a4da" is an example value of form query=bundle:digest.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS "byte-rate=none" means the findings query was asked and nothing answered (e.g. -e utf8).
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS "" (empty string) means nothing was asked.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS holds one query=bundle:digest item per findings query the compile ASKED, in the fixed query order, joined with ';'.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS uses query=none where the analysis declares nothing for this compile's encoding.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS is the empty string when no reader asked.
docs/spec/findings.md section 5 is the grammar of <PREFIX>_FINDINGS and the digest's byte layout.
In <PREFIX>_FINDINGS, bundle is the analysis whose block ANSWERED.
The <PREFIX>_FINDINGS digest covers exactly what the readers consumed, so two artifacts built from the same rates carry the same stamp.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS is written after every reader has run, beside the rx_info definition rather than with its prologue siblings, so an ask made while the engine body is emitted is recorded.
<PREFIX>_FINDINGS HAS an rx_info mirror, rx_info.findings, which equals it byte for byte.
The analysis bundle name is plain text in the artifact: a binary built under a user's analysis discloses its name.
<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS (abi 58) reports how many run compares the overlap row wrote.
<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS is on every artifact, both engines.
<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS is an activity count that section (b) keeps VM-only elsewhere, but it is stamped on both engines because the mechanism it counts (the run compare, tuning.md 2.38) is both engines'.
The run compare writes the DFA scan's run term and run pre-check as well as the VM's literal runs and island chains.
Since MEMFN M1b (2026-10-07, no abi event) the run compare is pcrec-memory-functions' (memfn/src/runcmp.c), and the kit writes the <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS line, as the first of its three lines.
The <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS value is an unquoted integer.
#define RX_RUN_WORDS 1 /* or 0, or any count */ is the form of the <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS stamp.
<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS is the number of literal-run compares the artifact writes as word compares, counting each compare once whatever engine wrote it.
The overlap row writes word compares for an exact run of length 3, 5-7 or 9-15.
Since abi 59 the words row writes a masked run as a word compare (tuning.md 2.39) and is counted in <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS.
Any other exact run compare is a memcmp and is not counted in <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS.
<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS is 0 on every artifact that writes no word compares, and under -fno-run-overlap.

<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS is written after the engine body, beside the rx_info definition (<PREFIX>_FINDINGS' placement), because a DFA artifact's compares sit in file-scope blocks emitted after the prologue.
<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS is a COUNT, for _VM_LIT_RUNS' reason.
A consumer may NOT conclude anything about the answers from <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS; they are identical either way.
<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS has no rx_info mirror (D77).
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS and <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC (abi 63, 2026-10-05) report what the search-code kit rendered and which libc functions the artifact calls.
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS and <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC are on every artifact, both engines.
The <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS/_MEMFN_LIBC pair is written by pcrec-memory-functions (memfn/, D146/D147).
The <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS/_MEMFN_LIBC pair sits directly after <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS.
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS is "none" iff the artifact is byte-identical (stamp lines aside) to its own -fno-memfn-simd compile.
Otherwise <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS lists the ids of the forms that make the artifact differ, comma-joined in site order.
A site that cascades between ISA levels carries its forms in <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS as ID@LEVEL+LEVEL.
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS ids and level names are OPAQUE: a consumer buckets on none/not-none and never parses an id.
SIMD is off by default and no SIMD form exists yet, so <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS is "none" on every artifact until the kit's first SIMD-on form ships (D147 addendum 10, Q55).
CHECK: A scalar-layer kit change (one that moves bytes at the default build) does NOT change <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS.
A scalar-layer kit change is attributed by its abi event and its --memfn=no-NAME deny row.
A consumer that must tell two same-abi builds apart records the build recipe (abi, pcrec commit, argv).
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC is "none" or the names of the C library functions the artifact's code calls, sorted in byte order, distinct, comma-joined with no space.
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC is a source-level inventory of the WHOLE artifact (search code, variable resolver, an --emit-main driver, --trace output; comments and string literals excluded).
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC is not a promise of a dispatched call: a name is listed even where the compiler later inlines or folds that call.
A memcpy of a constant 1-8 bytes (a register load, e.g. the literal-run word loads <prefix>_wN) is not listed in <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC.
Data objects an --emit-main or --trace artifact references (stderr) are not functions and are not listed in <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC.
A consumer may conclude that a SIMD-off artifact whose <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC lists memchr delegates that search to the C library's own dispatch.
Neither <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS nor <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC carries a kit version or the kit's vocabulary number, so a kit release that moves no emitted byte moves neither.
Neither <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS nor <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC has an rx_info mirror (D77).
Checked by C11 (make test-memfn-stamps, tests/memfn/run_libc_census.sh): over a corpus-wide sample every artifact carries both _MEMFN_FORMS and _MEMFN_LIBC lines.
Checked by C11: <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC equals the undefined function symbols of the artifact's -O0 -fno-builtin object minus the constant-size memcpy loads.

CHECK: The identity half of the _MEMFN_FORMS check compares default against -fno-memfn-simd (tuning.md 2.43), reported "identical (no SIMD form)" while no SIMD form exists, running from R4c when the -fno-memfn-simd/-fmemfn-simd switch exists.
CHECK: The movers half of the _MEMFN_FORMS check (-fmemfn-simd against SIMD-off) stays unreached until a SIMD form exists.
<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES (abi 71, 2026-10-09, D155 addendum 2) reports how many bytes of the artifact sit under a CPU-level guard.
<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES is on every artifact, both engines, written by pcrec directly after <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC.
<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES is an unsigned integer (e.g. #define RX_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES 0ULL).

<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES is the number of bytes the search-code kit wrote between its simd_open and simd_close sink calls (the #if <level> blocks a SIMD-on form adds: per-level helpers and the guarded arms of its selector).
<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES is counted in the unit every pcrec length decision uses: comment bytes -fno-comments dropped are included, and the symbol prefix is counted at a fixed width.
Neither -fno-comments nor -p changes the <PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES value.
<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES is 0ULL on every artifact that holds no such block, which is every artifact today: no SIMD form exists and -fmemfn-simd is inert (tuning.md 2.43).
A consumer may conclude from <PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES the artifact's size beyond its SIMD-off compile.

The SIMD-guarded bytes are invisible to every pcrec size decision: the VM entry-shape knee and <PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES, the size term and its ladder, and the D84 caps (limits.md section 8) all read the length minus these bytes.
Turning SIMD on moves no rung, no ladder step, no refusal and no other stamp's value; <PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES is where the difference stays visible.
There is no aggregate budget on <PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES (D155 addendum 2): each SIMD row bounds its own guarded bytes.
<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES has no rx_info mirror (D77).
Checked by make test-memfn-guarded (tests/memfn/run_simd_guarded.sh): every artifact of a corpus sample carries the _SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES line.
Checked by make test-memfn-guarded: the _SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES value is at most the sum over the SIMD forms <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS lists of each form's declared bound (0 while the value is "none").

A test-only build writing a synthetic guarded block through the same sink calls must produce artifacts equal to the plain build's, block and stamp value aside (arithmetic and decision neutrality of _SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES).

Family (b) capacity and activity macros stay VM-only: <PREFIX>_VM_RUNGS, _VM_STRATS, _VM_PRUNES, _VM_PRUNE_CEILING, _VM_CALL_SPLICED/_LINKED, _VM_ROOT_MINW, _VM_FRAMELESS, _VM_ALT_ISLANDS, _VM_CLS_FOLDS, _VM_LIT_RUNS, _VM_CLS_KIT, _VM_START, the budget macros and the frame/trail sizes.
Family (b) macros report what the VM DID (per quantifier, per call site, per frame); a DFA artifact has no such activity to report and does not carry them.
<PREFIX>_VM_START reports where an attempt may begin.
<PREFIX>_VM_START is a closed three-token selection stamp, on every VM artifact (hybrids included) and never defined on a pure-DFA artifact.
<PREFIX>_VM_START has exactly three values: "anchored", "gstart", "unanchored".
<PREFIX>_VM_START "anchored": every alternative of the whole pattern begins with ^ (outside multiline) or \A, so only offset 0 can start a match.
<PREFIX>_VM_START "gstart": every alternative begins with \G, so only the caller's own search_from can start a match.
<PREFIX>_VM_START "unanchored": nothing was proved, or -fno-vm-anchor-bound was given.
Either non-"unanchored" <PREFIX>_VM_START value means the emitted search loop stops after ONE attempt (tuning.md 2.25).
The <PREFIX>_VM_START fact is pcrec_start_anchor's, derived from the AST above either engine.
The DFA's own start_max is the same fact on the other engine, legible there through <PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "attempt"; the two vocabularies are deliberately one.
A consumer may NOT read <PREFIX>_VM_START "unanchored" as "this pattern is not anchored": it is the safe answer of a conservative analysis.
A denied build, a backreference-leading pattern and a genuinely unanchored pattern all report <PREFIX>_VM_START "unanchored".
From the non-"unanchored" <PREFIX>_VM_START values a consumer may conclude a fact about the artifact's loop, never a promise about run time.
<PREFIX>_VM_START has no rx_info mirror, on <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE's precedent, because no consumer reads the fact at run time today (D77).
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS (OPT-VMFL) is family (b), for _VM_CALL_SPLICED's reason: it is what the emitted program turned out to CONTAIN, not a decision the compiler made before emitting.
There is no frameless mode anywhere upstream of the emitter.
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS is 1 or 0 (e.g. #define RX_VM_FRAMELESS 1).
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS is 1 iff the artifact's VM program emits no RX_PUSH site and no linked call, i.e. the fail label has no pop-and-resume goto * dispatch; 0 otherwise.
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS is unconditional on every VM artifact, hybrids included, and never defined on a pure-DFA artifact.
Both <PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS values are spelled, never one omitted, because a fact readable by a macro's absence is a discriminator that was removed from two checks (OPT-1's _FAST_FRAMES precedent).
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS is a scalar boolean and not a mask: "did any site emit a push" is a whole-artifact fact with no per-quantifier axis to mix.
The masks (_VM_RUNGS, _VM_STRATS, _VM_PRUNES) are masks because the rung/strategy/clamp is chosen per A_REP and a scalar would lie on a mixed artifact.
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS has no rx_info mirror, on <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE's precedent (D77); the trigger to add one is the same one RX_DFA_TABLE's entry names, as a struct append moving no existing offset.
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS reports a second fact about the same artifact (CC-DIFF STEP 1), deliberately the same macro rather than a new one.
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS 1 additionally means the artifact's eight VM entry-chain statics carry static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) (at abi 17); 0 means none of them does.
A separate stamp <PREFIX>_VM_INLINE_CHAIN was considered and rejected: it would carry the same value as _VM_FRAMELESS by construction, since the emitter derives both from the one has_push bool.
A consumer that wants to know whether the VM entry chain is inlined reads <PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS, qualified by <PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE.
CHECK: Since CC-DIFF STEP 2 (2026-09-04), <PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS 1 is a necessary and no longer a sufficient condition for the entry-chain inline attribute; <PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE carries the rest.
A frameless artifact may carry the inline attribute on all eight entry-chain statics (<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE inline or forward).
A frameless artifact may carry the inline attribute on seven statics with the matcher noinline (<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE shared).
A frameless artifact may carry the inline attribute on none (<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE plain), which AUTO selects above the size term where the forward rungs are illegal.
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS 1 means the artifact is ELIGIBLE for the entry-chain inline attribute; <PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE says what was actually emitted.
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS 0 means none of the entry-chain statics carries the inline attribute; a framed artifact is plain by construction and there is no second route to 0.
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE and <PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES (CC-DIFF STEP 2, 2026-09-04) are family (b), for _VM_FRAMELESS's reason.
There is no entry-shape mode upstream of the emitter: the rung is chosen where the program has just been emitted, from the program's own size and what it turned out to contain.
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE has values "forward", "plain", "shared", "inline".
<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES is an unsigned long long integer (e.g. 646ULL).
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE names the rung the emitter took for the artifact's six entries.
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE "plain": one body, six framed entries.
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE "shared": one out-of-line body behind three forwarding entries.
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE "forward": three bodies in the three _in entries, three forwards.
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE "inline": six bodies (what STEP 1(a) shipped).
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE is a closed token (as <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL is); a consumer cannot bucket on prose, and the value set is fixed at four by the emitter's own enum.
<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES is the artifact's emitted VM program size in bytes: the exact quantity VM_INLINE_CHAIN_MAX_BYTES was compared against when AUTO chose the rung.
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE and <PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES are unconditional on every VM artifact, hybrids included, and never defined on a pure-DFA artifact.

Since abi 54 (K79), <PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES is measured at the canonical prefix length of two bytes: the program is emitted under a two-byte placeholder prefix and the caller's -p spelling is written afterwards (limits.md "Size limits and the prefix").
<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES is the program's length as it reads at -p rx, the same under every prefix, and the entry-shape rung chosen is the same under every prefix.
Four artifacts can stamp <PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE "plain" for four different reasons (framed, forward-illegal above the term, tiered, or asked for), so the shape alone does not distinguish them.
<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS separates the framed reason for "plain"; the program size (<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES) against the stamped limit separates the rest.
<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE and <PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES are scalars, not masks: the entry shape is a whole-artifact fact with no per-A_REP axis to mix.
Neither <PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE nor <PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES has an rx_info mirror, on RX_DFA_TABLE's precedent (D77).

<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS (ENG-ISL STEP 1, 2026-09-03) is family (b), for RX_ALTCLS_FACTORED's reason: what the emitted program turned out to CONTAIN, decided alternation by alternation in src/gen/emit_vm.c.
There is no island mode anywhere upstream of the emitter.
<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS is an integer count (e.g. #define RX_VM_ALT_ISLANDS 1, or 0, or more).

<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS is the number of the artifact's flat alternations that the VM lowered as an ALTERNATION ISLAND (a trie dispatch over the alternation's literal alternatives) rather than as vm_alt's serial resume chain (tuning.md 2.20).
<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS is unconditional on every VM artifact, hybrids included, and never defined on a pure-DFA artifact; 0 is spelled as readily as any other value.
A DFA artifact carries no <PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS decision, since the DFA route determinizes the same trie for every alternation whether or not anyone names it.

<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS is a COUNT and not a boolean, on RX_ALTCLS_MERGES/_FACTORED's precedent: the island is selected per alternation, so a pattern with two can take it for one and decline the other.
<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS is not a mask, for _DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS' reason: it is a whole-artifact total with no per-alternation axis to mix.
A consumer may conclude from <PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS that the artifact dispatches its alternations by byte rather than by trying them in turn.
With islands, the artifact's cost on a wide alternation does not scale with the branch INDEX of the winner.
With islands, the artifact's emitted size does not depend on the ORDER the alternatives were written in.
A consumer may NOT conclude anything about the answers from <PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS: an island reports the same alternative, in the same backtracking order, as the chain.
<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS has no rx_info mirror, on <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE's precedent (D77); the trigger to add one is the same one RX_DFA_TABLE's entry names.

<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS (FORM-CHAR STEP 1, 2026-09-05) is family (b), for _VM_ALT_ISLANDS' reason: what the emitted program turned out to CONTAIN, decided pool class by pool class by the fold rows of src/gen/clskit.c's class-form table (byte-fold, byte-fold-default).
There is no fold mode anywhere upstream of the emitter.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS counts a VM program's folds only; a DFA scan edge's fold (abi 53, --tune=-2/-1) is reported by <PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "fold".
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS is an integer count (e.g. #define RX_VM_CLS_FOLDS 6, or 0, or any count).
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS is the number of the artifact's VM class-pool entries whose membership test takes the ASCII-FOLD shape (tuning.md 2.22).
The ASCII-FOLD shape is a two-member set differing only in bit 0x20, both members letters, tested as (byte | 0x20) == lower with NO 32-byte bitmap table emitted for it.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS is unconditional on every VM artifact, hybrids included, and never defined on a pure-DFA artifact; 0 is spelled as readily as any other value.
The DFA route's class machinery (byte-class partition, scan-edge bodies) never consults the byte-fold row, so <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS has nothing to report there.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS is a COUNT and not a boolean, on _VM_ALT_ISLANDS' precedent: the shape is selected per pool class, so a pattern can mix fold-pair positions with bitmap classes.
Distinct pool entries are distinct sets, so distinct fold classes carry distinct compare constants, which lets a structural check hold the <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS number to the artifact's own text.

A consumer may conclude from <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS that the artifact's caseless-letter positions test by one or-mask-and-compare each (no load) and that it carries that many fewer 32-byte class tables.
A consumer may NOT conclude anything about the answers from <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS: the fold compare and the bitmap read are the same predicate over the set's own two bytes.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS has no rx_info mirror, on the same precedent and reason as <PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS (D77).
<PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS (OPT-LITSCAN S2a, abi 41) is family (b), for _VM_CLS_FOLDS' reason.
<PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS is an integer count (e.g. #define RX_VM_LIT_RUNS 5, or 0, or any count).
<PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS is the number of literal-run compares the artifact's VM program writes.

A literal run counted in <PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS is a run of three or more one-byte literals in a concatenation (OPT-LITSCAN F5, abi 43, D127, narrowed from two: a two-byte run reads cheaper as its own two-node byte chain, tuning.md 2.31).
An alternation island's single-child trie chain is also counted in <PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS, unaffected by F5's floor (its own mechanism).
Each counted literal run is compared as one bounds check and one run compare (tuning.md 2.31, 2.38).
Since abi 58 a run compare is a constant-length memcmp or, at the lengths gcc decomposes, two overlapping word compares.
<PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS is unconditional on every VM artifact, hybrids included, never defined on a pure-DFA artifact.
<PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS is 0 under -fno-lit-run.
<PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS is a COUNT, for _VM_CLS_FOLDS' and _VM_ALT_ISLANDS' reason.
A consumer may NOT conclude anything about the answers from <PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS; they are identical either way.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT (CLS-TREE S4, 2026-09-29, abi 48) is family (b), for _VM_CLS_FOLDS' reason.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT is an integer count (e.g. #define RX_VM_CLS_KIT 1, or 0, or any count).
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT is the number of distinct class-matcher functions (<prefix>_wcls<N> and, since abi 51, <prefix>_class_kit<N>) the artifact's VM program calls.
A wcls matcher is a wide class tested as one decode and one matcher.
A class_kit matcher is a byte class tested by the kit's K form at --tune=-2/-1, where the kit is smaller than the class's table (tuning.md 2.33).
A DFA scan edge's kit matcher (<prefix>_<machine>_scankit<N>) is not counted in <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT; it is reported by <PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "kit".
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT is emitted on every VM artifact, hybrids included, and never on a pure-DFA artifact.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT reads 0 under -fno-cls-kit.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT reads 0 under -e byte at --tune=0/+1/+2.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT is a COUNT, for the entries above's reason.
A consumer may NOT conclude anything about the answers from <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT; they are identical either way.
A consumer may NOT conclude which form a matcher took from <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT: that is --emit-ir's consume row and the matcher's own text.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS (OPT-CLSPACK, 2026-09-30, abi 48) is family (b), for _VM_CLS_FOLDS' reason.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS is 0 or the shared table's atom count, 1..64.

<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS is non-zero exactly when the artifact's VM program tests its table-read byte classes through ONE shared byte->atom table (<prefix>_class_atoms, tuning.md 2.34); then it is the number of atoms that table numbers.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS 0 means a 32-byte bitmap per class (or no table-read class at all).
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS is emitted on every VM artifact, hybrids included, and never on a pure-DFA artifact.
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS reads 0 under -fno-cls-pack.
A consumer may NOT conclude anything about the answers from <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS; they are identical either way.
<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES and <PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL (OPT-1, 2026-08-25) are family (b) macros.
<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES and <PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL report the capacities the un-suffixed entries' FAST TIER runs on (sections 3, 10.9).
<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES and <PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL are on every VM artifact, single-tier ones included.
<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES is an integer (e.g. 47, tiered: below the stamped default).
<PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL is an integer (e.g. 71).
<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES == <PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES is the statement "this artifact has one tier", and it is the only spelling of it.
A single-tier artifact arises when the stamped default already fits a page.
A single-tier artifact arises when the slot array alone does not fit a page.
A single-tier artifact arises when the scaled fast tier would be too small to be worth two runs.
A single-tier artifact arises under -fno-tiered-entry.
A consumer that needs to distinguish the causes of a single tier reads rx_info.flags and the pattern, not a missing macro.
<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES and <PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL are never absent on a VM artifact.

<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES and <PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL are family (b), not section 10.4: section 10.4's five macros (both engines) are arithmetic a caller must do in order to call an _in entry, whereas no entry takes a fast capacity and no caller sizes anything from one.
<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES and <PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL are .c-private like the budget macros, so a consumer reading only the header does not see them.
A consumer's code should not branch on the tier boundary.
On a DFA artifact the (b) macros are absent: no budget macros and no _VM_RUNGS/_VM_STRATS/_VM_PRUNES masks.
A --no-captures build defines RX_NCAPS and the two RX_ALTCLS_* stamps.

Since ABI-NS (2026-08-18, D60), unconditionally on every artifact regardless of engine: the give-up code space, the unset sentinel, PCREC_ENGINE_DFA/PCREC_ENGINE_VM, and the nine D46 stamp bit constants (PCREC_VM_RUNG_*/PCREC_VM_STRAT_*/PCREC_VM_PRUNE_*) are defined.
The universal constants on a DFA artifact have the same "reserved but unreachable" shape the give-up codes had.

A DFA artifact does NOT carry the budget macros and the three OR'd masks RX_VM_RUNGS, RX_VM_STRATS, RX_VM_PRUNES; they stay VM-artifacts-only because a DFA artifact has no per-quantifier rung/strategy/clamp decision to summarize.
RX_ENGINE_WHY stays VM-only: it names the construct that FORCED the VM, and a DFA artifact was not forced.
A DFA artifact's rx_info.engine_why is NULL, so RX_ENGINE_WHY's absence mirrors the struct.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL (OPT-4, 2026-08-29) is the same decision as <PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY expressed as a TOKEN, a different macro on purpose.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY is prose, written for a person and allowed to name an offset, a construct or a build outcome; a consumer cannot bucket on it.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL has a CLOSED value set.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL is unconditional on every artifact, both engines, like _ENGINE and unlike _ENGINE_WHY (D81: a fact stamped only when interesting is a hint, and "selected" is a fact).
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL and <PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY are written from one derivation at src/opt/select_engine.c's single fit site; neither is parsed to produce the other.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "selected": auto chose on the AST and nothing overflowed; the common case, on both engines.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "forced": the caller named --engine=vm or --engine=dfa, so auto selected nothing.

<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "declined-nullable-default" (OPT-4.2, 2026-08-31): auto, nothing overflowed, and the ordinary hybrid's own exact prefilter language is nullable (matches the empty string), so the forward+reverse DFA pair would admit a zero-length match at every position and could never dismiss one.

Since abi 68 (NULLABLE-ANCH), "nullable" for <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "declined-nullable-default" is the empty_admits fact: a pattern whose every empty match crosses a non-multiline start AND end anchor (e.g. ^(\s+)*$) is not declined and reads "selected".
Since abi 69 (DEC-VAR-ATTRIB) a ${...} pattern is never declined with "declined-nullable-default": its variable turns the prefilter off before nullability is asked, and it reads "selected".
-fprefilter overrides the "declined-nullable-default" decline.
An explicit --engine=vm reads <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "forced" (F-B2) rather than "declined-nullable-default".
Under <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "declined-nullable-default" no rung is involved and no prefilter survives; it is the general form of "declined-nullable" off the rung it is scoped to (tuning.md 2.17).
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "overflowed-dfa": auto, the DFA was to be the ENGINE, its build overflowed a cap, and no prefilter survived the fallback (SEL-1).
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "overflowed-prefilter": auto, the VM was already chosen for another reason, and only its auto-selected prefilter's DFA overflowed, so the prefilter was dropped.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "collapsed-prefilter": auto, a DFA build overflowed a STATE cap, and the SEL-1 retry KEPT a prefilter by rebuilding it from the count-collapsed language (tuning.md 2.5, 2.17).
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "declined-nullable": auto, a SEL-1 or OPT-4 retry offered the count-collapsed prefilter and it was DECLINED because the collapsed language is nullable (matches the empty string).
Under <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "declined-nullable" no prefilter survives and the artifact is the one this compile produced before that retry existed (tuning.md 2.17, OPT-4.1).
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry": an emitted-SIZE cap (not a DFA state cap) refused the exact artifact and a retry rebuilt a smaller one that SHIPPED.
The rungs reaching "size-cap-retry" are the size-cap ladder's (limits.md section 8), and the artifact's own axis stamps say which.

On a VM hybrid, "size-cap-retry" is LIM-1/OPT-4's rung with the count-collapsed prefilter surviving, legible as <PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER with <PREFIX>_PREFILTER_LANG_WHY "count-collapsed" (tuning.md 2.17).

On a VM hybrid, "size-cap-retry" may be the ladder's last rung (PF-DROP, D135) with the prefilter DROPPED, legible as <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none" with <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_WHY "size cap retry, hybrid N > CAP".
The <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_WHY "size cap retry, hybrid N > CAP" string records the refused artifact's bytes and the cap it exceeded, and is the only "none" that stamp is written beside.
On a DFA artifact, "size-cap-retry" is K53-SELRETRY's optional-contributor drop where the anchored match-here machine was dropped (tuning.md 2.15), legible as <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "search-filter".
On a DFA artifact, "size-cap-retry" may be K59-PREMUL's premultiplied-table drop, legible as <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE off "premultiplied".
size-cap-retry is distinct from "collapsed-prefilter", which is the SEL-1 DFA-state-cap rung's own success; the rungs are offered under different conditions in compile_driver's retry loop.
The last five <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL values (overflowed-dfa, overflowed-prefilter, collapsed-prefilter, declined-nullable, size-cap-retry) are all "fell back".
The first four fallback values share one _ENGINE_WHY prose string ("dfa overflowed: ...") and differ in what SURVIVED.
size-cap-retry has its own prose behavior: _ENGINE_WHY is unaffected by an emitted-size refusal, so it still reads whatever forced the VM or stays absent on a plain DFA build.
A consumer wanting only "did this compile fall back?" tests for all five fallback <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL values; one wanting cost or which cap reads which.
declined-nullable-default is NOT among the five fallback values: nothing overflowed on that path; it is an ordinary compile whose own prefilter a policy declined and sits beside "forced"/"selected".

<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "declined-nullable" and "overflowed-dfa" are not the same outcome: both artifacts carry <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none", but the first is a rescue refused as useless and the second one that was not available.
A consumer measuring what the collapse rung buys must not count "declined-nullable" as a case where the rung had nothing to offer.
declined-nullable-default and "declined-nullable" are the same policy on two different populations, kept as two values (OPT-4.2, 2026-08-31).
declined-nullable says a ladder RUNG offered a rescue and it was refused; "declined-nullable-default" says there was never a rung: the ordinary hybrid's own exact prefilter was declined.
A size-rung retry that SUCCEEDS (collapsed prefilter survived) stamps <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry" (LIM-1, D90, 2026-08-30), not "selected".

Before "size-cap-retry" existed, a successful OPT-4 size rung stamped "selected" because dfa_disabled is never set on this rung: the DFA build itself succeeded and the whole artifact was refused by an emitted-size cap.
A refused rescue (nullable) reads "declined-nullable"; one that shipped reads "size-cap-retry"; only a genuinely unremarkable compile reads "selected".
K53-SELRETRY (2026-09-10): a second rung joined <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry" rather than minting a third value.

An artifact carrying the optional anchored match-here machine (<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped") that a size cap refuses is re-emitted without it (limits.md section 8, "The optional-contributor drop") and reads "size-cap-retry".
Without the "size-cap-retry" value, \p{L} under -e utf8 would stamp "selected" while the artifact is slower than an unconstrained build's.
Which contributor a retry dropped is read off the artifact's own axis stamps, not off a second <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL value.
The two "size-cap-retry" rungs cannot both fire on one compile (the first requires a VM hybrid, the second a DFA artifact), so the pair is exact.
Under a force form <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL reads "forced" and says nothing about a retry: "forced" is tested first and wins outright.
--engine=dfa (or --engine=vm) on a pattern a size cap refused reads <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "forced" however the compile was rescued.
Measured at K53-SELRETRY: --engine=dfa --features unicode-props -e utf8 -- '\p{L}' compiles and stamps <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "forced" where the same pattern under auto stamps "size-cap-retry".
The OPT-4 size rung's own witness stamps "forced" under --engine=vm.
The size-cap retry is not gated on auto, unlike SEL-1's engine fallback (which changes the engine a caller demanded); a drop rung changes only an entry-point form inside the requested engine.
No flag lets a caller demand the dropped anchored machine (-fno-anchored-dfa is deny-only).
A consumer needing the WHY on a forced compile reads <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH and gets "this artifact has no anchored machine" without its cause.
Distinguishing the five populations of the <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH value needs <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL, which a force form has spent.
<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL has no rx_info mirror, on <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE's precedent (D77); the trigger to add one is a named consumer rather than symmetry.
rx_info.engine_why continues to mirror the PROSE (<PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY), not the token.
RX_ENGINE_WHY can also name a build outcome, not only a construct (SEL-1, 2026-08-28).

Under --engine=auto, a DFA build that overflows a cap (state count, table entries, the K7 element budget; tuning.md 2.11) is a selection outcome rather than a refusal, and the artifact falls back to the VM.
A SEL-1 fallback artifact stamps its outcome in RX_ENGINE_WHY the same way every other forcing reason is stamped.

Since OPT-4 (2026-08-29) a SEL-1 fallback can appear beside RX_VM_PREFILTER "hybrid" rather than only beside "none": the fallback's first rung rebuilds the prefilter from the count-collapsed language instead of dropping it.
RX_VM_PREFILTER_LANG_WHY "dfa overflow retry, exact nfa N" says the prefilter was rebuilt from the count-collapsed language (tuning.md 2.5, 2.17).
Example RX_ENGINE_WHY for a DFA overflow: "dfa overflowed: >32000 states at pattern offset 0".
The offset in an overflow RX_ENGINE_WHY is not tied to any one AST node (it is a property of the whole compile) and reads 0 by convention, the same position the underlying pcrec_ctx_fail reports at.
If the engine choice is ALSO forced by a real construct (a capture request, a VM_ONLY registry row), that reason wins the RX_ENGINE_WHY stamp on the ordinary first-wins rule.
In that case, the overflow's own effect on the prefilter (dropped, RX_VM_PREFILTER "none") still applies independently, through a fact RX_ENGINE_WHY does not carry.
A consumer MAY #if on RX_ENGINE, because it is unconditional on every artifact.
A consumer #if-ing on RX_VM_RUNGS or a budget macro (any family (b) macro) writes code that does not compile against a DFA artifact.
Measured by listing every #define in a fresh build of each artifact kind: family (b) macros are absent from a DFA artifact.
The per-artifact SUMMARY macros live in the generated .c, not the .h; the universal PCREC_* constants live in the .h.

In the split form (the CLI default) the .h carries the whole unprefixed universal set from the shared PCREC_RX_ABI_H block (section 2): the four give-up codes, PCREC_UNSET, the two engine constants, the nine D46 stamp bit constants.
In the split form the .h also carries <PREFIX>_NCAPS, on every artifact including a DFA-only one.
Measured on one VM build and one DFA build: nineteen #defines in each .h, identical except RX_NCAPS's value; twenty-six in the VM .c.
CHECK: Before ABI-NS the .h had eight #defines and the .c thirty-five; the difference was the eleven macros that moved (PCREC_ENGINE_DFA/_VM new, plus nine D46 bit constants).
The #if use case for the universal constants no longer needs a self-contained build: they reach a consumer's TU through the ordinary #include "<name>.h".

The per-artifact SUMMARY macros (RX_ENGINE, the masks, the budgets) are emitted into the .c only, so reading them requires a self-contained artifact (header_name == NULL) or being the generated .c itself.
Whether the summary macros should also be emitted into the header is an open design question, not settled.
Example: the observability macros on a captures-default build of 'a(b|c)+d' are listed below; the #define lines are the artifact's, the /* ... */ annotations are the document's.
RX_ENGINE is "vm" on a captures-default build of a(b|c)+d and mirrors rx_info.engine.
RX_ENGINE_WHY is "capture group at pattern offset 1" on that build.
RX_VM_PREFILTER is "hybrid" or "none" on a VM artifact.
RX_VM_PREFILTER_WHY (e.g. "size cap retry, hybrid 1026588 > 1000000") is emitted ONLY where the size-cap ladder dropped the prefilter (PF-DROP).
RX_VM_PREFILTER_LANG is "exact" or "count-collapsed", reports the count-collapse axis ONLY (the end proof is _VM_RESEED "exact"), and is emitted only where _VM_PREFILTER reads "hybrid" (OPT-4).
RX_VM_PREFILTER_LANG_WHY (OPT-4) says which of five reasons produced the _VM_PREFILTER_LANG value (e.g. "no counted repeat").
RX_VM_RUNGS is a bitmask of which per-quantifier rungs the artifact actually uses: CURSOR/FRAMES_BOUNDED/FRAMES_UNBOUNDED/REVDET/COUNTER.
RX_VM_STRATS is a bitmask of POSSESSIVE/BACKTRACKING strategies.
RX_VM_POSS_ARMS (ART-POSS-ARMS) is a bitmask of which possessify ARM a positive verdict needed: 0x1 A0, 0x2 A1, 0x4 B.
RX_VM_PRUNES is a bitmask of CLAMPED/UNCLAMPED (MRL).
RX_VM_PRUNE_CEILING is a string; e.g. "prefilter-window" on the a(b|c)+d hybrid example.
On a DFA artifact (measured on (?:[a-z]+)@(?:[a-z]+)) RX_ENGINE is "dfa", mirrors rx_info.engine, and is unconditional.
RX_DFA_SCAN is "unanchored" or "attempt" (or "empty") on a DFA artifact.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER is "byte-class" on the email-specimen DFA artifact.
RX_DFA_TABLE is "premultiplied" on the email-specimen DFA artifact.
A VM hybrid (measured on a(b|c)+d) carries RX_ENGINE "vm", RX_ENGINE_WHY, RX_VM_PREFILTER "hybrid", RX_DFA_SCAN, RX_DFA_PREFILTER and RX_DFA_TABLE all at once.
On a VM hybrid, RX_DFA_SCAN, RX_DFA_PREFILTER and RX_DFA_TABLE describe the DFA that the VM runs ahead of its program, and its candidate-start filter and table encoding.
RX_DFA_SCAN names WHICH DFA SCAN the artifact CONTAINS.
RX_DFA_SCAN has three values: "unanchored", "attempt", "empty".
RX_DFA_SCAN "unanchored" is the O(n) forward+reverse table pair (D7).
RX_DFA_SCAN "attempt" is the per-start-position computed-goto loop a ^/\A-bearing pattern takes.

unanchored and "attempt" are different loops with different cost curves, and nothing else a consumer can read distinguishes them: both stamp RX_ENGINE "dfa" and both set rx_info.engine to PCREC_ENGINE_DFA.
RX_DFA_SCAN "empty" (DD-13c, 2026-08-25) is a third shape, not a special case of the other two.

A pattern the start analysis proves can match nothing (\B\b, \b\B, \d\b\w, a\bb, and their ^-anchored spellings) compiles to a search body that is one return 0: no table, no loop, no skip, on either engine.
CHECK: Before DD-13c, provably-empty artifacts stamped the name of the loop the emitter would have written ("unanchored", or "attempt" when anchored).
RX_DFA_PREFILTER reads "none" on every RX_DFA_SCAN "empty" artifact, because there is no scan for a filter to be part of.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER names the candidate-start mechanism the artifact carries.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER has eleven values, the whole set.

RX_DFA_PREFILTER "none": no candidate-start filter: the start state ACCEPTS (start_acc; no skip is sound; the largest cause, e.g. a*, .*, \bx*), every position is a candidate, or the artifact provably matches nothing.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "memchr": ONE candidate byte value at offset 0; a memchr() replaces the steps.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "byte-class": several candidate bytes at offset 0; a 256-entry <prefix>_can_begin_match bitmap walk.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "memchr-bounded": the memchr form under a $/\Z/\z view or a word context: bounded at n - 1 and WITHOUT the early return 0.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "byte-class-bounded": the bitmap form under the same view/word context, bounded at n - 1.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "offset-set" (OPT-K): a SET of (offset, byte-set) tests, one scanned for and the rest verified on each candidate; see RX_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "offset-set-bounded": the offset-set form under the same view/word context, bounded at n - 1.

RX_DFA_PREFILTER "run-pinned" (OPT-LITSCAN S1, abi 36): the pattern's necessary run (RX_REQ_RUN) sits at a fixed offset from every match's start and the scan already runs on the run's own scan member there, so the candidate test verifies the WHOLE run as one compare (the offset-set block with the run as one term).
Under RX_DFA_PREFILTER "run-pinned" the run pre-check is not emitted (RX_REQ_WHY "dominated").
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "run-pinned" is removed by -fno-run-prefilter OR -fno-offset-skip.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "run-pinned-bounded": the run-pinned form under the same view/word context, bounded at n - 1.

RX_DFA_PREFILTER "first-memchr-bounded" (START-SET stage 3, the DFA hat, abi 64, tuning.md 2.42): on a SEEDED machine (a \b, a lookbehind, a (?m) context) whose plain skip would test the start state's escape set E, the skip tests the pattern's START SET T (the start_set fact) instead, where T is a proper subset of E; here ONE byte, a memchr().
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "first-memchr-bounded" is bounded at n - 1 like "memchr-bounded"; a skip that moved re-seeds the scan state from the byte before its landing.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "first-memchr-bounded" is removed by -fno-start-set.
RX_DFA_PREFILTER "first-class-bounded": the same as first-memchr-bounded with several start-set bytes: a 256-entry <prefix>_start_bytes table walk, bounded at n - 1.
The DFA hat (first-*-bounded forms) has no unbounded form: a seeded machine always carries the D11 bound.
<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS (OPT-K, abi 9) is on every artifact the four RX_DFA_* stamps (_DFA_SCAN, _DFA_PREFILTER, _DFA_TABLE and itself) are on.
<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS names WHICH offsets the filter tests, as a comma-separated ascending list of byte offsets from the candidate's own start with '*' marking the one the scan searches for.
Example: RX_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS "0,8*,13" (the uuid shape).
RX_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS "none" is the value for every other value of _DFA_PREFILTER.
<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS reads "none" on every artifact whose _DFA_PREFILTER is not one of the two offset-set or two run-pinned values, and is non-"none" on exactly those four values (an iff).
On a run-pinned value, <PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS lists every offset the test covers, the run's own offsets individually (router /user|/users: "0*,1,2,3,4").
On a run-pinned value the scan may be offset 0 ("0*"), which no other value's scan is.

<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS is a second stamp rather than a widening of _DFA_PREFILTER because _DFA_PREFILTER's value is the emitter's chosen FORM (a fixed, countable set of strings) while this one is a fact about the individual machine.
Offset 0 is always a member of <PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS: it is the test the four older values already make (on a run-pinned value, as the scan, a verify, or a byte of the run).
<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH (ENG-ABS, abi 10) is on every DFA artifact and, unlike the four stamps above, NOT on a VM hybrid.
<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH names which of section 3.2's two forms the artifact's <prefix>_match and <prefix>_match_caps take.
<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped": the artifact has its own anchored machine, run from ctx->pos.
<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "search-filter": the unanchored search is run and non-ctx->pos starts are rejected.
<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped": the artifact carries a THIRD machine (the forward tables WITHOUT the start-anywhere self-loop) and runs it from ctx->pos.
Under <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "unwrapped" there is no later start to reject, no backwards pass, and a failing probe stops at the first byte that cannot continue a match beginning here.
<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "search-filter": the entry runs <prefix>_search and rejects any match whose start is not ctx->pos.

<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "search-filter" has FIVE populations: _DFA_SCAN "attempt"; _DFA_SCAN "empty"; an anchored machine that exceeded a DFA cap (a selection outcome, never a refusal); any build under -fno-anchored-dfa; and (K53-SELRETRY, 2026-09-10) an artifact whose anchored machine was dropped to fit under an emitted-size cap.

Only the size-cap-dropped population of <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH "search-filter" is distinguished by <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL (it reads "size-cap-retry"); the other four read whatever their engine selection was, ordinarily "selected".
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE (OPT-5, abi 13) is on every artifact that CONTAINS a DFA scan: DFA artifacts and VM hybrids, the same iff as _DFA_SCAN/_DFA_PREFILTER/_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS/_DFA_TABLE.
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE names how the DFA scan tests the class of a SCAN EDGE.

A scan edge is a maximal run of states differing only in how many bytes of one fixed class have been counted, replaced by a bounded cursor loop and DELETED from the transition table (tuning.md 2.18; src/opt/scanedge.c).

An edge's test is the class-form table's answer for its class at the artifact's --tune position and the scan site (src/gen/clskit.c ROWS/TAB_ROWS, abi 53, D139 item 2), spelled by the same emitters a VM program's class read uses.
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE has exactly six values: "none", "range", "fold", "bitmap", "kit", "mixed".
RX_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "range" is exemplified by the test (unsigned)(b - 97) <= 25u.
RX_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "none" means no machine carries a collapsible run.

<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "none": the artifact carries no scan edge; four causes, none of them a failure: no machine has a collapsible run; _DFA_SCAN "attempt" (states are code labels, step is a computed goto, no loop-carried table load to shorten); _DFA_SCAN "empty" (body is one return 0); any build under -fno-scan-edge.
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "range": every edge in the artifact tests a CONTIGUOUS byte range (the class table's byte-range row), emitted inline against immediates.
A "range" edge test is b == c, or b <= hi from 0, or otherwise (unsigned)(b - lo) <= span u (the VM's own spelling since abi 53), so the loop touches no memory but the subject.
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "fold" (abi 53): at --tune=-2/-1 only, every edge's class is an ASCII case pair on the byte-fold row, tested inline as (b | 0x20) == x.
At --tune 0/+1/+2 a scan edge's fold pair is a "bitmap" (D138 Q1: the default fold is held for both sites until its measurement rules).
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "fold" never occurs under -fno-cls-fold.
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "bitmap": at least one edge's class is on the byte-table row, and the table selection's scan-table row gives it a 256-byte membership table read.
Under "bitmap" the loop-carried register is still the cursor, which is the property the transform is for; the memory reference is the price.

<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "kit" (CLS-TREE S2, abi 52): at --tune=-2/-1 only, every edge's class is on the class-form table's byte-kit row (its kit matcher, written at the edge's two test sites, is smaller than its 256-byte table; abi 53, D139 item 1).
Under "kit" the edge test calls a static inline kit matcher <prefix>_<machine>_scankit<N> in place of the table (tuning.md 2.33).
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "kit" never occurs at --tune 0/+1/+2 and never under -fno-cls-kit.
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "mixed": an artifact-level composition (as RX_DFA_TABLE's): the artifact's machines took more than one form; the choice is per EDGE and a machine may carry up to four.

<PREFIX>_DFA_START (OPT-5 STEP 2, abi 16) is on every artifact that CONTAINS a DFA scan: DFA artifacts and VM hybrids, the same iff as <PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE and the four stamps beside it, and NOT <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH's narrower one.
<PREFIX>_DFA_START is a family (a) selection fact: defined iff the artifact contains a DFA scan, its value names the object axis J selected.
<PREFIX>_DFA_START names which of two forms the scan entry takes when it recovers the match START.
RX_DFA_START "pinned": the start is search_from, by compile-time proof.
RX_DFA_START "reverse-pass": a second, backwards scan finds the start.

<PREFIX>_DFA_START "pinned": the forward machine's start state accepts UNCONDITIONALLY (at every position, under every position view, in every class context), so a match exists wherever the search begins and D3's accept-pruning removed the start-anywhere self-loop from every accepting closure before the first byte was read.
Under "pinned", every accept the forward loop records belongs to a thread that began at search_from, and the post-loop block writes that offset directly.

A "pinned" artifact carries NO reverse machine: no transition, accept or byte-class table, no stay tables, no scan-edge membership tables, no <prefix>_reverse_* accessor block and no reverse scan loop.
<PREFIX>_DFA_START "reverse-pass": the artifact carries its reverse machine and walks it backwards from the match end to find the furthest-back accepting position.

reverse-pass covers every artifact whose start state does not accept, or whose accept depends on the position or the upcoming byte, or which seeds into a state that may be dead, or whose scan is "attempt" or "empty", or any build under -fno-start-pinned.
The "pinned" and "reverse-pass" forms are ANSWER-IDENTICAL and differ only in cost and size.

caps[0][0]'s contract is unchanged under both <PREFIX>_DFA_START forms, including section 3.1's "every offset written to caps is an ABSOLUTE offset into s, never relative to startpos" and the zero-length-match-is-a-success convention; the pinned form depends on both.
rx_info.search_form mirrors <PREFIX>_DFA_START.
docs/spec/tuning.md section 2.19 is the <PREFIX>_DFA_START axis and docs/design/opt5_step2_twopass.md the proof.

A pinned search can still return 0 on some calls: a search at startpos > 0 on a machine whose start state depends on a context byte can begin in a state with no live closure, records no accept, and "no match begins here" is the correct answer.
The emitted artifact keeps that no-live-closure test and names it load-bearing above the line.

The _DFA_START iff differs from the other stamps' in the fact: the other _DFA_* stamps describe a DFA scan (a VM hybrid contains one, so they appear on hybrids), while <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH describes the artifact's <prefix>_match ENTRY.
On a hybrid the <prefix>_match entry is the VM's own anchored body, which the <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH axis does not describe and whose value set it does not share.
<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH is defined on exactly the artifacts whose RX_ENGINE is "dfa".
rx_info.match_form is NULL on every artifact whose engine is not "dfa", hybrid included.
<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH is the entry a caller reads to know whether it is in section 3.2's worst case.
The two -bounded values of <PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER are a REAL difference in what the mechanism buys, not a spelling.
Under a view, a skip may not pass the position whose accept has not been evaluated yet, so every skip stops one byte short and the memchr arm loses its early-out.
DD-13 (b) measured the (?:P)\z spelling's loop as strictly weaker than the plain form's on the same candidate table (docs/dev/plan.md).
A consumer that cannot tell the -bounded values apart would attribute the difference to the pattern.
RX_ENGINE, RX_VM_PREFILTER, RX_DFA_SCAN, RX_DFA_PREFILTER and RX_VM_PRUNE_CEILING are scalar macros for a per-artifact-wide verdict.
RX_VM_RUNGS, RX_VM_STRATS and RX_VM_PRUNES are bitmasks, used when the axis is decided per-quantifier and a single scalar would misreport a mixed pattern.
RX_VM_POSS_ARMS (ART-POSS-ARMS, abi 66) is the per-ARM half of RX_VM_STRATS' POSSESSIVE bit.
RX_VM_POSS_ARMS bit 0x1 is A0, a lookahead-born gate in the follow valued with nothing known on its left.
RX_VM_POSS_ARMS bit 0x2 is A1, a gate valued by the loop's own LAST characters' polarity.
RX_VM_POSS_ARMS bit 0x4 is B, a backreference's first character read from its groups.
An RX_VM_POSS_ARMS bit is set when that arm was NEEDED for some positive possessify verdict.
For arm A1, the RX_VM_POSS_ARMS bit means the verdict was decided by A1 alone; for A0 and B, it means the same compile with that arm denied counts fewer positive verdicts.
RX_VM_POSS_ARMS is 0x0u where no arm was needed, including every artifact built with both arms denied: a denied arm's bit is 0 by construction (tuning.md 2.44/2.45).
RX_VM_POSS_ARMS is emitted on every VM artifact, never on a DFA-only one.
The RX_VM_POSS_ARMS bit values are defined in this document only; they are not named constants in the PCREC_RX_ABI_H block.
Of the VM macro block, everything but RX_ENGINE is VM-artifacts-only.

RX_DFA_SCAN, RX_DFA_PREFILTER, RX_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS, RX_DFA_TABLE, RX_DFA_SCAN_EDGE and RX_DFA_START are the DFA scan's own selection facts and appear on every artifact that CONTAINS such a scan (DFA artifacts and VM hybrids).
RX_DFA_TABLE (OPT-3), RX_DFA_SCAN_EDGE (OPT-5 STEP 1) and RX_DFA_START (OPT-5 STEP 2) all join the "contains a DFA scan" iff unchanged.
RX_DFA_MATCH (ENG-ABS) does NOT join the "contains a DFA scan" iff: it is a fact about an ENTRY, so its iff is RX_ENGINE "dfa".

Since ABI-NS (2026-08-18, D60) the named bit constants (PCREC_VM_RUNG_*, PCREC_VM_STRAT_POSSESSIVE/_BACKTRACKING, PCREC_VM_PRUNE_CLAMPED/_UNCLAMPED) are not emitted per-prefix; they live in the shared unprefixed PCREC_RX_ABI_H block (section 2), emitted once and unconditionally on every artifact including a DFA-only one.
Only the three OR'd masks RX_VM_RUNGS, RX_VM_STRATS, RX_VM_PRUNES stay per-prefix and VM-only, since their value is the one genuinely per-artifact fact.
Two more D46 stamps are NOT VM-only, and a DFA-only artifact carries them too: RX_ALTCLS_MERGES and RX_ALTCLS_FACTORED.
RX_ALTCLS_MERGES is the count of alternation runs merged into one class.
RX_ALTCLS_FACTORED is the count of alternation runs prefix-factored.
RX_ALTCLS_MERGES and RX_ALTCLS_FACTORED are emitted before either engine is built, so they appear on a capture-free pattern's DFA artifact as well.
Measured on a --no-captures build: RX_ALTCLS_MERGES and RX_ALTCLS_FACTORED appear on a DFA artifact.
rx_info.flags and the compile-time macros answer different questions, and the masking rule applies to only one of them.
rx_info.flags records the REQUEST: the PCREC_* option bits exactly as compiled, with the testing/tuning denials masked OUT.
Axis denials are masked out of rx_info.flags because an axis that changes no answer must not make two identically-behaving artifacts differ in their reflection surface.
The observability macros record what the emitter DID, and visibly move when a denial is exercised.
Measured on (x)(?:a|bc)+d: building -fno-possessify moves RX_VM_STRATS from 0x1u (POSSESSIVE) to 0x2u (BACKTRACKING) while the emitted rx_info.flags value is unchanged.

Between the default and -fno-possessify builds of (x)(?:a|bc)+d, the whole rx_info initializer is identical except frame_capacity, which moves because denying possessification really does cost a frame.
To see what was ASKED FOR, rx_info.flags cannot be used for a masked axis; to see what HAPPENED, read the macro.
Every axis bit is masked from rx_info.flags except the named kept set; the rule is general and derived, not a list (tuning.md section 2, "THE rx_info.flags RULE"; K92).

The set of masked bits and per-flag reasoning live in lib/pcrec.h's own comments (indexed by lib/CLAUDE.md), which is where to look to see which bits legitimately vanish from rx_info.flags on a round trip.
